newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Credireal bid specs published Friday.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Credireal bid specs published Friday.

text.p: Minas Gerais state government on Friday published the bid specifications for the August 7 sale of its bank Credireal.

The state is offering a total of 1.06 billion shares, of which are 763.3 million voting shares and 299.6 million preferred stocks, equivalent to 99.962 percent of Credireal's voting capital or 99.941 percent of the bank's total capital.

Credireal's base price for the auction of a majority stake in the bank was set at 130.8 million reais or 123 reais per 1,000 stocks, the tender document said. Minority shareholders will also be allowed to offer their shares at the auction.
Bank employees are allowed to buy 10 percent of the voting shares on offer, with a 50 percent discount. They may reserve their shares between July 14 and July 24, it added.
Eight financial institutions have prequalified for Credireal's auction, which will take place at the Minas Gerais-Espirito Santo-Brasilia Stock Exchange (BOVMESB).

They are Credit Commerciale de France's Banco CCF Brasil, BankBoston's Brazil unit, General Electric's General Electric Capital Corp, Banco Industrial e Comercial, Banco Noroeste, Companhia de Investimentos Latinoamericana, Tabal Participacoes and Varejo SA Administracao e Participacao.

Credireal, formally known as Banco de Credito Real de Minas Gerais SA, is the second Brazilian state-owned bank due to be privatized. The first was Rio de Janeiro state bank Banerj, which was bought by Brazil's second largest private bank Banco Itau late June.
